modules.name: trigger-lab-store (TriggerLab god object)
modules.responsibility: Single Svelte-runes application store that owns the entire authoring model (graphs, presets, effects, canvas scenes, buses, transport, setlist) and exposes ~207 mutation methods plus ~42 accessors to every UI surface.
public_interface: 28 $state fields (graphs, graphNames, presets, canvasScenes, buses, pads, bpm, velocity, playing, galleryBlock, settingsBlock, envTarget, ...)

~207 methods: node CRUD (addNode/removeNode/connect/disconnect/reconnect/spliceOnDrop), param setters (setMode/setScope/setChance/setDelayMs/...), graph CRUD, section/song/show CRUD delegators, clipboard/paste, controller + backup + MIDI-learn commands, routing setters
modules.notes: Largest file in repo; 109 files outside trigger-lab reference the lab, most through this store. Many methods are one-line delegators to store/* pure helpers or to the extracted controllers (shallow pass-throughs), while persistence/hydration/WS-sync sections are genuinely deep.

modules.name: store pure helpers (store/*)
modules.responsibility: Stateless, immutable transformation helpers the store calls to compute new graph/edge/param/project values and to classify legal wiring operations.
modules.notes: Well-factored: small interfaces over real rules (cycle detection, band port remapping). ids.ts holds module-level mutable id state — a hidden global.

modules.name: hydration & migration pipeline
modules.responsibility: Normalizes and forward-migrates persisted graphs — unioning builtin effects/presets, materializing linked nodes, and running the gen3 envelope/env-map/alias/play-type/mod-source-split/integrity migrations.
modules.notes: Migration chain is append-only; each new gen adds another pass over every graph.

modules.name: persistence & schema versioning
modules.responsibility: Defines the localStorage schemas (authored state, show library, song library) with serialize/deserialize/coerce plus versioned migrations including the 1-based hoop-target shift.
modules.notes: Two version axes (authored v2, shows v2, songs v1) coexist; hoop migration duplicated in shape with hydrate's migrations.

modules.name: show & song library model
modules.responsibility: Models reusable library songs and shows — closure extraction, namespacing, ref resolve/detach, delete planning, server reconciliation, and compiling the authored model into an engine Show.
modules.notes: Two near-identical sync classes (shows vs songs) and two near-identical library CRUD sets — prime duplication territory.

modules.name: extracted store controllers
modules.responsibility: Host-injected rune-owning collaborators carved out of the store (shows/songs, section arrangement, controller monitor/test, MIDI learn, save-status timing) that the store re-exposes through delegating accessors.
modules.notes: Real extraction, but every method is mirrored back onto the store as a forwarder, so the store's surface never shrank.

modules.name: simulation engine (Sim)
modules.responsibility: Deterministic offline voice/graph simulator: compiles a TriggerGraph into blocks, resolves hits against trigger sources, and advances voices with envelope/LFO modulation on mono/poly buses.
public_interface: types Block/PlayBlock/AllBlock/RandomBlock/SequenceBlock/SwitchBlock/ChanceBlock/ToggleBlock, Bus, Voice, Section, LogEntry, EffectDef, Preset, Scope, PlayMode
modules.notes: sim.envelopes.ts is almost purely re-exports of core voice types — a barrel, not a module. 14 sim.*.test.ts files, including a gen3-parity suite.

modules.name: clipboard document format
modules.responsibility: Versioned copy/paste document format for graphs, sections, songs, and patches — build, serialize, parse with typed errors, id remapping on paste, and a diff view for incoming patches.
modules.notes: Own v1→v2 migration axis, separate from persistence's and hydrate's.

modules.name: canvas scenes
modules.responsibility: Models user-authored canvas scene documents and projects each one into a virtual effect definition plus default preset so scenes appear in the normal effect pickers.

modules.name: engine sync / transport link
modules.responsibility: Keeps the browser model and the server engine in agreement — transport state signature diffing and computing the resync message list when a restored project differs from the live one.

modules.name: live rendering & kit model
modules.responsibility: Builds the lab's pixel/kit geometry model and composites sim voices into an RGB frame buffer for the 3D preview.
modules.notes: fixtures.ts is seed data masquerading as a module; effects/presets defined here rather than in core.

modules.name: effect thumbnails
modules.responsibility: Renders animated per-effect preview thumbnails on a shared rAF ticker with a cached dot-grid projection of the kit.

modules.name: signal preview & envelope geometry
modules.responsibility: Pure math for modulation-source preview traces and ADSR editor hit-testing/dragging, plus the SVG views that draw them.
modules.notes: Geometry cleanly split from view — the strongest seam in the UI layer.

modules.name: dock telemetry
modules.responsibility: Normalizes sim-side and server-side voice/level telemetry into one dock view model with exponential smoothing, plus input-binding liveness badges and stat formatting.
modules.notes: stat-format.ts (18 LOC) is a shallow two-function module.

modules.name: clip editing UI
modules.responsibility: Modal surfaces for choosing an effect and editing a play node's preset, parameters, and per-param envelopes.
modules.notes: Both bind directly to the god store rather than to props — no injectable seam.

modules.name: trigger-lab test corpus
modules.responsibility: Vitest suites covering the store (35+ files), sim behaviour, persistence migrations, clipdoc round-trips, and UI geometry — roughly half the LOC in scope.
modules.notes: Store tests are split by feature (store.delay, store.lfo, store.shows…) while store/ has a parallel set — two organizing schemes for the same subject; jscpd flags 58 duplicated lines between persistence.songlibrary.test.ts and store/song-library.test.ts.

seams.why: Each extracted controller takes a host interface of callbacks, so its behaviour is testable and substitutable without touching the store.
WS transport is injectable at construction — tests can swap the client without a live server.
Clock injection makes save-status timing deterministic in tests.
Migrations take lookup functions instead of reaching into the store, keeping them pure.
Id minting on paste is a pluggable strategy, allowing deterministic remap tests.
Module-level mutable id registry (reserveId/reserveIds) is process-global state shared by store, clipdoc paste, and library import — no way to scope or reset it per store instance.
Storage is touched directly via `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'` guards in two different modules rather than behind one injected storage port.
Components consume the TriggerLab instance directly instead of a narrow prop/view-model, so no UI behaviour can be varied or tested without the whole store.

seams.at: migration chain across persistence.ts (hoop/song migrations) and store/hydrate.ts (gen3 migrations)
seams.why: There is no single registered migration pipeline; each new schema generation appends a bespoke pass in whichever of the two files happens to own the shape.
Two reconciliation classes with parallel ReconcilePlan/SongReconcilePlan shapes and no shared abstraction — a change to reconcile semantics must be made twice.
A shared exported rAF ticker object means thumbnail animation timing cannot be substituted or paused per consumer.
EFFECTS/PRESETS/BUSES/PADS are hard-coded seed data imported by store, sim, hydrate and render alike — the effect catalog has no registry seam.

suspicions.hunch: Adding a node kind, a persistence field, a controller command, or a paste context all force edits to this one class — it is the repo's single highest-churn file and almost every unrelated concern converges on it.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.svelte.ts section/song/show delegators to sectionsCtl and showsCtl (e.g. get/set activeSectionId, sectionClipboard, newShow, saveShow, renameSong)
suspicions.hunch: The controller extraction added a layer without removing the old surface — dozens of methods are pure forwarders, so the store still has the full API and the split bought navigability, not decoupling.

Both suites appear to build the same library fixtures and assert overlapping round-trip behaviour, which suggests the production code is likewise split across persistence.ts and store/song-library*.ts along an arbitrary line.

suspicions.where: store/show-library-sync.ts vs store/song-library-sync.ts; store/shows.ts (withShow/renameShowIn/planDeleteShow) vs store/song-library-refs.ts (withLibrarySong/renameLibrarySongIn/planDeleteLibrarySong)
suspicions.hunch: Two libraries of named, id-keyed, delete-planned entities implemented twice with parallel names — likely one generic library module in disguise.

suspicions.where: parallel test-organisation schemes: store.<feature>.test.ts (35+ at top level) vs store/<feature>.test.ts
suspicions.hunch: The same subjects (canvas-scenes, shows, song-library, value-switch, system-toasts, graphs, ids) have suites in both places; some pairs may be near-copies testing the same code path twice.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.svelte.ts graph keys — pad graphs keyed `drumId:zone`, authored graphs keyed `graph-<n>`; store/seed.ts padKey()
suspicions.hunch: Two semantically different identifier kinds share one bare `string` type and are parsed by convention, so a pad key and an authored key are indistinguishable at every call site.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/sim.graph-compilation.ts NODE_KINDS + nodeHasInput/nodeHasOutput/nodeHasModInput/nodeHasParams/nodeIsModSource, and the ~25 per-kind setters in store.svelte.ts (setMode/setScope/setChance/setSwitchOn/setDelayMode/setBandCutoff/…)
suspicions.hunch: Node-kind capability is decided by five separate predicate functions plus a fan of kind-specific setters; adding a kind means finding every one of them.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/sim.envelopes.ts (75 LOC, essentially all `export type X = voice.X` re-exports)
suspicions.hunch: A file that only aliases core types adds an indirection layer with no behaviour; same smell in parts of sim.ts's re-export block.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/NOTES.md ("throwaway model probe … delete this directory" with all three verdicts still TBD)
suspicions.hunch: The directory is documented as a disposable prototype but is now ~13k LOC referenced by 109 files — the doc is stale and may hide genuinely abandoned probe-era code (fixtures.ts EFFECTS/PRESETS, render.ts, kit.ts) alongside production paths.

Effect definitions and frame compositing live in an app-level lab directory while AGENTS.md declares effects/compositor belong to packages/core — the web app may be carrying a second, divergent effect catalog.

suspicions.where: apps/web/src/lib/trigger-lab/store.svelte.ts localStorage persistence effect (~1234-1300) and writeStoredLibrary in shows-controller.svelte.ts:90
suspicions.hunch: Write-through localStorage caching guarded only by `typeof localStorage === 'undefined'`; quota-exceeded or serialization failure on a large show library likely throws inside a $effect with no fallback.

suspicions.where: store/trigger-routing.ts partial types (DrumTransformPartial, KitGlobalPartial, HoopConfigPartial, OutputPartial) and their matching store setters
suspicions.hunch: Four parallel `apply*(project, partial)` functions each mirrored by a store method suggest one Project-patch operation split four ways by data shape.

suspicions.where: three independent version axes: persistence.ts (VERSION 2 / SHOWS_VERSION 2 / SONGS_VERSION 1), clipdoc.ts (CLIPDOC_VERSION 2), store/hydrate.ts gen3 migrations
suspicions.hunch: A single model change (e.g. a new node field) must be threaded through three unrelated migration mechanisms; drift between them is likely already present in hoop-target handling, which appears in both persistence.ts and hydrate.

items.coverage_notes: Read fully or substantially: store/*.ts export surfaces (all non-test files), sim.* module headers, persistence.ts, clipdoc.ts, hydrate.ts, and the export lists of every non-test .ts in the directory. I read only the first ~420 lines of store.svelte.ts plus a full method-name inventory (207 methods, 42 accessors, 28 $state fields) — the bodies of the persistence effect, WS sync, paste/materialize, and node-editing sections are UNREAD, so depth judgements there are inferred from names and import graph. The six .svelte components (ClipSettings, EffectGallery, EnvelopeEditor, EnvelopeEditorView, EffectThumb, SignalFace, StatusBar, ~1900 LOC) were NOT read at all — their responsibilities and the "binds directly to the store" claim are inferred from the store's popup state fields and the 109-file external reference count, not verified. No test file bodies were read; the duplication suspicions restate the jscpd signal plus the filename-parallelism pattern rather than confirmed copies. LOC figures per module are summed from wc and are approximate for grouped modules.
